**2B.1 Research Note: Andrés Manuel López Obrador in 2024**

Best-supported reading: **yes, largely**. The 2024 record shows repeated preference for diplomacy, de-escalation, and negotiated restraint where peaceful options clearly existed. I found **no direct 2024 evidence** that AMLO treated force as the preferred first option in a foreign-policy crisis.

| Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable page URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| [La política se inventó para evitar la guerra, afirma presidente sobre conflicto en Medio Oriente](https://amlo.presidente.gob.mx/la-politica-se-invento-para-evitar-la-guerra-afirma-presidente-sobre-conflicto-en-medio-oriente/) | Presidente de México | 2024-04-13 | <https://amlo.presidente.gob.mx/la-politica-se-invento-para-evitar-la-guerra-afirma-presidente-sobre-conflicto-en-medio-oriente/> | AMLO explicitly said politics exists to avoid war, urged that the Iran-Israel conflict not escalate, described war as irrational and harmful, and called for peace and fraternity. This is the clearest direct evidence of choosing de-escalation when a peaceful alternative existed. | 2B.1, 1B.8, 1B.2 |
| [US, Mexico to clamp down on illegal immigration, leaders say](https://theprint.in/world/us-mexico-to-clamp-down-on-illegal-immigration-leaders-say/2062785/) | Reuters | 2024-04-30 | <https://theprint.in/world/us-mexico-to-clamp-down-on-illegal-immigration-leaders-say/2062785/> | Biden and AMLO agreed to coordinate immediate measures to reduce irregular border crossings while protecting human rights. This is a concrete example of compromise and bilateral diplomacy instead of coercive escalation. | 2B.1, 1B.8 |

That is direct evidence of preferring diplomacy and de-escalation over force. | 2B.1, 1B.1, 1B.2, 1B.4 |
| [With World at Delicate Crossroads, Disarmament Committee’s Responsibility ‘Immense’, Says General Assembly President During Robust Debate](https://press.un.org/en/2024/gadis3737.doc.htm) | United Nations, Meetings Coverage and Press Releases | 2024-10-08 | <https://press.un.org/en/2024/gadis3737.doc.htm> | Mexico’s representative urged fewer warheads, more disarmament, and less rhetoric threatening nuclear use, and rejected the idea that nuclear weapons are part of the solution. This is multilateral evidence of choosing restraint and diplomacy over escalation. | 2B.1, 1B.1, 1B.2, 1B.4 |
| [Mexico chairs OPANAL General Conference](https://www.gob.mx/sre/prensa/mexico-chairs-opanal-general-conference?idiom=en) | Secretaría de Relaciones Exteriores | 2024-11-28 | <https://www.gob.mx/sre/prensa/mexico-chairs-opanal-general-conference?idiom=en> | Mexico reaffirmed the Treaty of Tlatelolco and a world free of nuclear weapons while OPANAL participants reiterated disarmament and dialogue with nuclear-weapon states. This shows continued preference for negotiated restraint and institutional channels. | 2B.1, 1B.4, 1B.6, 1B.7 |
| [Mexico freezes relations with US, Canadian embassies which criticized judicial reform](https://www.investing.com/news/commodities-news/mexico-to-pause-relationship-with-us-embassy-after-judicial-reform-comments-president-says-3589198) | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-08-27 | <https://www.investing.com/news/commodities-news/mexico-to-pause-relationship-with-us-embassy-after-judicial-reform-comments-president-says-3589198> | AMLO paused relations with U.S. and Canadian embassies after criticism of his judicial reform. This is adverse evidence of confrontation and reduced compromise, though it is not evidence of force-first war-making. | 2B.1, 1B.7, 1B.10 |

**Assessment**

- Strongest positive evidence: AMLO’s April 2024 statement on the Iran-Israel crisis, plus repeated diplomatic/disarmament messaging from Mexico’s foreign ministry and UN/OPANAL channels.
- Strongest negative evidence: the embassy pause after judicial-reform criticism, which shows confrontation but not war-first behavior.
- Net judgment: **AMLO mostly chose diplomacy and de-escalation over force in 2024.**

**Search gap**

- I did not find a direct 2024 case where AMLO had to choose between force and a credible peaceful alternative in a conventional military crisis.
- So this is a strong diplomatic-restraint read, but not a hard test of battlefield crisis decision-making.
